original_test_intent: Verify each Type 4 L3 Cache Handle is the defined no-information sentinel or resolves to the correct Type 7 last-level cache representation for that processor, including approved socket/die sharing, and remains correct after reboot.
original_method: Capture complete raw/decoded Type 4 and Type 7 structures, resolve non-sentinel L3 references by handle, validate target level/type/capacity and socket/die/cluster sharing against the platform topology, reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: A user approves the last-level-cache representation, per-socket/die sharing policy and reboot plan. Complete handle-graph validation is automatable.
required_inputs: Approved socket, die or cluster sharing granularity
Expected Type 7 L3 level, role and capacity plus no-information sentinel policy
Approved reboot and OOB recovery plan
safety_requirements: Use read-only SMBIOS collection; do not alter cache controls, NUMA configuration, CPU state or firmware.
Preserve complete Type 4 and Type 7 raw/decoded structures and numeric handles.
Resolve every non-sentinel handle to exactly one Type 7 record and verify L3/last-level attributes rather than accepting a stable string.
Do not assume one L3 record per socket; chiplet or die-level cache representations require the approved platform model.
Stop on dangling/wrong-type references, unapproved sharing/capacity drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Build and validate the L3 relationship graph with target attributes and approved sharing, then compare it before/after reboot.
Do not change cache/NUMA settings, infer undocumented topology or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the expected last-level cache representation and sharing/capacity rules.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The label is relevant, but grep neither resolves the handle nor validates that the target is the expected L3/last-level record and sharing topology.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture full raw/decoded Type 4 and Type 7 inventories, resolve each L3 reference and verify target level/type/capacity plus socket/die sharing.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The L3 Cache Handle scope, Type 4 script and 10/10-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a handle-indexed SMBIOS graph, explicitly process the sentinel, resolve all L3 references and compare Type 7 attributes and approved socket/die/cluster sharing before and after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 4 and Type 7 systems, including multi-die processors.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, BIOS, CPU/socket/die topology and parser/dmidecode versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 4 cache-handle and Type 7 cache-information semantics, CPU/platform cache topology documentation and installed tool documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds referential integrity and L3-specific capacity/sharing interpretation while preserving the source field.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Improves coverage by detecting wrong targets and wrong last-level-cache grouping.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Expected L3 graph, attributes and sharing granularity.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware may aggregate physical cache slices; OS cache IDs are supporting evidence only unless an approved mapping exists.

project_override_considerations: The approved representation may be per socket, die, CCD/tile or another documented group; it must be explicit and must not be normalized into a generic one-handle-per-CPU rule.
expected_evidence: Approved L3 graph, sharing/capacity/sentinel rules and platform/tool versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 4/Type 7 structures and resolved handle graph
Target-level evidence for cache level, type, capacity and approved group membership
Approved reboot/health evidence and equivalent post-reboot comparison
Engineer verdict with documented topology rationale

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item and persistence criterion consistently target the L3 handle; topology details are project inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The relationship is readable and machine-checkable after its expected platform model is supplied.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Adds Type 7 resolution and L3-specific sharing/capacity validation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keeps the correct graph approach but corrects capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE and separates final verdict.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Accounts for multi-die last-level-cache representations instead of assuming a universal socket topology.

review_improvement: Detects stable but dangling or mis-grouped last-level cache metadata and avoids false failures on documented multi-die representations.
independent_technical_reasoning: Once the platform's L3 representation is approved, graph construction, target checks and persistence comparison are entirely software-controlled.
